question: What does the term tele-nursing specifically refer to within healthcare delivery?

options.A: Nursing practice executed entirely through telecommunication technologies
options.B: The automated computerized diagnosis of complex hospital diseases
options.C: Physical bedside nursing enhanced by electronic patient beds
options.D: Electronic hospital record keeping done by administrative staff

explanation: Tele-nursing specifically denotes the use of telecommunication tools by registered nurses to deliver care, triage, and education remotely. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h1)

question: How does tele-health primarily benefit patients living in remote or underserved geographic regions?

options.A: By guaranteeing that emergency surgery can be performed at home
options.B: By entirely eliminating the need for any prescription medications
options.C: By replacing all local primary health clinics with automated kiosks
options.D: By bridging physical distance to reduce travel burdens for clinical guidance

explanation: Remote populations gain access to medical advice and follow-up without enduring long, expensive journeys to centralized urban facilities. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which tele-health modality involves transmitting medical images or data to a clinician to be reviewed later without a live conversation?
explanation: Store-and-forward technology relies on asynchronous transmission where data is saved and sent for later evaluation by an expert. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h2)

question: A clinic wants to track a hypertensive patient's daily blood pressure from their home using a cellular cuff that automatically uploads readings to a portal. What modality is being used?
explanation: Continuous home tracking of physiological metrics using automated digital devices falls under remote patient monitoring. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is a primary clinical duty performed by a tele-nurse during a virtual encounter?

options.A: Surgically implanting remote monitoring hardware sensors
options.B: Conducting structured symptom triage and patient assessment
options.C: Performing routine hospital structural engineering repairs
options.D: Manually manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs at a distance

explanation: Tele-nurses use specialized questioning and clinical judgment to evaluate incoming symptoms and determine the appropriate urgency of care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why is patient education regarding home diagnostic tools a critical responsibility for tele-nurses?

options.A: It ensures that data transmitted from home devices is accurate and reliable
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never need to see a doctor again
options.C: It is required primarily to sell medical hardware devices for profit
options.D: It removes all legal liability from the nursing licensing board

explanation: If patients do not operate blood pressure cuffs or glucose meters correctly, the remote data sent to clinicians becomes misleading and clinically unsafe. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which regulatory body maintains primary professional oversight over nursing practice standards in Nigeria?

options.B: Federal Ministry of Information and Culture
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating the standards of nursing and midwifery education and practice across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of applying data protection legislation, like the Nigeria Data Protection Act, to tele-health records?

options.A: To prevent patients from ever seeing their own medical history records online
options.B: To safeguard electronic health information against privacy breaches and unauthorized access
options.C: To ensure that tele-health software companies make high commercial profits
options.D: To speed up the internet bandwidth speeds across rural health outposts

explanation: Strict data laws ensure that sensitive patient health records transmitted digitally remain confidential and protected from cyber threats. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h4)

question: Which technique is recommended for verifying a patient's understanding of instructions given during a virtual health consultation?
explanation: Asking the patient to repeat instructions in their own words confirms whether the communication was successfully understood. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h5)

question: How must a nurse adapt their physical assessment skills when conducting a consultation entirely through a video link?

options.A: By skipping the assessment phase entirely if the patient owns a smartphone
options.B: By relying more heavily on structured verbal questioning and visual environmental observations
options.C: By asking a family member to perform all clinical diagnostic decisions
options.D: By performing standard physical percussion and palpation through the screen

explanation: Without physical access, the nurse evaluates the patient using targeted questions, active listening, and visual clues captured by the camera. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is considered a major infrastructural barrier to implementing reliable tele-health services in many developing regions?

options.A: Strict laws that ban all mobile phones from being used outdoors
options.B: Unstable electrical power grids and intermittent internet connectivity
options.C: An overabundance of advanced fiber-optic cables in rural villages
options.D: Universal free access to high-speed satellite broadband for everyone

explanation: Reliable tele-health requires consistent electricity and stable internet, both of which can be erratic in underserved settings. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary benefit commonly associated with successful tele-health adoption?

options.A: Completely eliminating all chronic illnesses worldwide
options.B: Expanding specialized clinical access for remote populations
options.C: Optimizing ongoing chronic disease monitoring routines
options.D: Reducing unnecessary travel burdens and associated costs

explanation: While tele-health improves management and access, it cannot cure or completely eliminate chronic diseases. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h6)

question: How are artificial intelligence tools beginning to assist tele-nurses in modern practice?

options.A: By performing physical bedside surgeries autonomously
options.B: By flagging abnormal remote monitoring data patterns early
options.C: By eliminating the need for any patient health records
options.D: By replacing human nursing licenses with automated bots

explanation: AI algorithms help analyze large streams of remote patient data to alert nurses to potential clinical deterioration before it becomes critical. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h7)

question: What impact do advancing wearable biosensor technologies have on remote patient monitoring?

options.A: They require patients to remain permanently tethered to hospital walls
options.B: They allow for the continuous tracking of advanced physiological biomarkers
options.C: They function exclusively without any power source or batteries
options.D: They make patient monitoring entirely obsolete and unnecessary

explanation: Modern wearable sensors capture sophisticated health metrics continuously, providing richer data for remote clinical evaluation. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h7)
